dialogue.content: （本日はよろしくお願いいたします！）
dialogue.English: (I look forward to our session today!)

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、よろしくお願いいたします
dialogue.English: Likewise, thank you for having me.

dialogue.content: こんにちは相談員です。本日はご相談ありがとうございます。早速ですが・年齢・性別・相談内容をお聞きしてもよろしいでしょうか？内容はどんなものでも構いませんので、ご自由にお書きください。なお、なんとお呼びすればよろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm the counselor. Thank you for reaching out today. To begin, may I ask your age, gender, and what you would like to discuss? Please feel free to share whatever is on your mind. Also, how would you like me to address you?

dialogue.content: ４０代 女 職場のこと名前は何でも良いです
dialogue.English: 40s, female, about my workplace. Any name is fine.

dialogue.content: 教えてくださいまして、ありがとうございます。それでは、相談者様とさせていただきますね。職場のご相談とのことですが、どのような内容になりますでしょうか？話せる範囲で結構ですので教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that with me. For now, I'll refer to you as 'the client.' You mentioned your concern is about your workplace. Could you tell me more about that? Please feel free to share only as much as you're comfortable with.

dialogue.content: 嫌がらせを受けてます
dialogue.English: I'm being harassed.

dialogue.content: それはお辛いですね。どのような嫌がらせなのか教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: I'm sorry to hear that. Could you tell me what kind of harassment you're experiencing?

dialogue.content: 何かする度に、ダメ出しされます
dialogue.English: Every time I do anything, I get criticized.

dialogue.content: ダメ出しをされてしまいますと、やる気も出なくなりますよね。
dialogue.English: When you're constantly criticized, it must be hard to stay motivated.

dialogue.content: なんで、そんなこと言われないといけないのかと言う気持ちになります
dialogue.English: It makes me feel like, 'Why do I have to put up with being told things like that?'

dialogue.content: 何かするたびに言われてしまったら余計にそういう気持ちにもなりますよね
dialogue.English: It's completely understandable to feel that way, especially when it happens every time you do something.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ダメ出しをされる方はどのようなお立場の方ですか？お一人でしょうか？
dialogue.English: What position is the person criticizing you in? Is it just one person?

dialogue.content: いろいろな人にです
dialogue.English: It's from many different people.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。それは、悩まれますよね。
dialogue.English: I see. That must be very distressing for you.

dialogue.content: 古株のバイトの人や、管理者、クライアントなど
dialogue.English: Veteran part-timers, managers, clients, and so on.

dialogue.content: みんなに言われます
dialogue.English: Everyone says it to me.

dialogue.content: そのような状況の中でも、相談者様は、我慢されてお仕事を続けて来られたんですね。
dialogue.English: And despite that situation, you've been enduring it and continuing with your work.

dialogue.content: そうです
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: いつ頃からそのような状況でいらっしゃるのですか？
dialogue.English: About how long have you been in this situation?

dialogue.content: 二年ぐらい前だったと思います
dialogue.English: I think it started about two years ago.

dialogue.content: ２年も前から、その状況に耐えていらっしゃったのですね。お辛かったでしょうね。
dialogue.English: So you've been enduring this situation for two years. That must have been very painful for you.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ２年前からとのことですが、何かきっかけはあったのですか？
dialogue.English: You mentioned it's been going on for two years. Was there anything that triggered it?

dialogue.content: 産休明けで、今の部署に配属されました
dialogue.English: After returning from maternity leave, I was assigned to my current department.

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Mhm.

dialogue.content: それからです
dialogue.English: That’s when it started.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。産休明けでの出勤は、それでなくても不安でしょうに。。。
dialogue.English: I understand. Returning to work after maternity leave is anxiety-provoking enough as it is...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ダメ出しとは、どのような内容なのですか？
dialogue.English: What kind of criticisms are they, specifically?

dialogue.content: 報告書のミス、お客様対応がとんちんかん、要領悪い、残業しすぎなどです
dialogue.English: Things like mistakes in reports, that my customer service is off the mark, that I’m inefficient, and that I work too much overtime.

dialogue.content: なんで、そこまで言われないといけないのでしょうか
dialogue.English: Why do I have to be told all that?

dialogue.content: そのように思われるのも、無理ないですよね。その思いを感じながらも、お仕事されていたのですね。
dialogue.English: It's no wonder you feel that way. You've been continuing to work while carrying those feelings.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 体調は大丈夫ですか？睡眠とか食事はちゃんととれられていらっしゃいますか？
dialogue.English: Are you doing okay physically? Are you getting enough sleep and eating properly?

dialogue.content: はい。もともと、テレビ観たりしてて睡眠時間は短いです
dialogue.English: Yes. I've always been a short sleeper because I watch TV and things like that.

dialogue.content: 食事も基本、ファーストフードです
dialogue.English: My meals are basically fast food, too.

dialogue.content: 子供も喜ぶので！
dialogue.English: My kids enjoy it!

dialogue.content: 体調が大丈夫なのであればよかったです。お子様喜ばれるのですね、それは嬉しいですね。
dialogue.English: I'm glad to hear you're feeling okay. It's wonderful that your children enjoy it; that must make you happy.

dialogue.content: ほか弁、マクドナルド、KFCのデリバリーは喜びます
dialogue.English: They get excited for bento takeout, McDonald's, and KFC delivery.

dialogue.content: お子様は、そのお食事が好きなのですね。
dialogue.English: So your children enjoy those meals.

dialogue.content: はい。私もです。
dialogue.English: Yes. So do I.

dialogue.content: 家族皆が喜びます
dialogue.English: The whole family enjoys it.

dialogue.content: そうですか。皆が喜ぶ食事いいですね。ご相談者様はお家ではくつろげるのでしょうか
dialogue.English: I see. It's wonderful to have meals that everyone enjoys. Are you able to relax when you're at home?

dialogue.content: 子供三人いて、ギャーギャー言ってますが、普通だと思います
dialogue.English: I have three children, and they're always making a racket, but I think that's normal.

dialogue.content: もともと、管理部門で雇われてたのに、一度目の産休が開けたら管理部門が本社へ移っていたので、現場仕事になりました。二度目の産休明けも現場仕事です。
dialogue.English: I was originally hired for the administrative department, but when I returned from my first maternity leave, the department had moved to the head office, so I was given on-site work. After my second maternity leave, it's still on-site work.

dialogue.content: こんな仕事しないといけないのか
dialogue.English: Do I really have to do this kind of work?

dialogue.content: 話が違う
dialogue.English: This isn’t what I was told.

dialogue.content: クライアントから報告書を理論的にまとめて下さいとか、しらんし
dialogue.English: Clients ask me to 'summarize reports logically,' and it's like, how am I supposed to know how to do that?

dialogue.content: お子様三人もいらっしゃるのですね。ギャーギャーいうのが普通だと思ってくださる相談者様に育てられて、お子様は幸せですね。管理部門から現場の仕事になったのですね。もともとの話とも違っていたのですね。それでは、しらん　とも思われますよね。
dialogue.English: You have three children. They must be happy to be raised by a mother who thinks their noisiness is normal. So you were moved from an administrative to an operational role, and that was different from what you were originally told. It makes sense that you would feel, 'How am I supposed to know how to do that?'

dialogue.content: バイトからは、しっかりして貰わないとクライアントに切られると言われるし
dialogue.English: And the part-timers tell me, 'If you don't get your act together, we'll be dropped by the client.'

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Mhm.

dialogue.content: なんで、そんなこと言われないといけないのでしょうか
dialogue.English: Why do I have to be told things like that?

dialogue.content: 産休明けでの出勤は間が空いていてそれだけでも不安なのに。。。元の話とも違う現場の仕事にもなってしまってそんなことを言われたら納得いかないですよね
dialogue.English: Returning to work after maternity leave is anxiety-provoking enough due to the time away... On top of that, to be placed in on-site work that differs from what was originally discussed and then be told such things—it's understandable that it wouldn't sit right with you.

dialogue.content: 社員なのだから、移動は当たり前にある会社って管理部門にいたから解ってることやろと言われます
dialogue.English: I get told, 'Since you're a full-time employee, you should know that transfers are a normal part of this company—you were in the administrative department, after all.'

dialogue.content: 出向でないし、会社は子育てとかの事情も考えてくれてるほうちゃうかと言わます
dialogue.English: They say things like, 'It's not a secondment, and isn't the company actually being considerate of your childcare situation?'

dialogue.content: ご相談者様は、ちゃんとご相談されたということですよね。それなのに、そんな言われ方をしたら不満のままですよね。
dialogue.English: So you're saying that you properly discussed this with them. And yet, to be spoken to like that must leave you feeling very dissatisfied.

dialogue.content: 相談？
dialogue.English: Discussed?

dialogue.content: すみません、相談ではなかったですかね。異動は当たり前で解っているだろう子育ての事情も考えてくれている方という回答があったということは、相談者様がのお気持ちをお話されたのかと思ってしまいました。
dialogue.English: My apologies, perhaps 'discussed' was the wrong word. When you received the reply that 'transfers are normal and they are considering your childcare situation,' I assumed that you had shared your feelings with them.

dialogue.content: いえ、「ええなぁ、社員は出向行かされて病んで帰ってくるのに、事務所勤務って優遇されてるよね」
dialogue.English: No, it's more like, 'Must be nice. Employees get sent on secondments and come back burned out, but you get preferential treatment working in the office.'

dialogue.content: とか
dialogue.English: Things like that.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。相談者様のお気持ちを知らないとはいえ言われたくなかったですね。
dialogue.English: I see. Even if they don't know how you feel, that's not something you should have to hear.

dialogue.content: 「会社的に、産休三回取って子育てしてる社員いますっていえるね」
dialogue.English: 'From the company's perspective, they can say, "We have an employee who took maternity leave three times and is raising her children."'

dialogue.content: とかです
dialogue.English: Things like that.

dialogue.content: そういうのであれば、産休明けに不安がない環境作りもしてほしいですね。
dialogue.English: If that's their attitude, you would hope they would also create an environment where you feel secure after returning from maternity leave.

dialogue.content: 事務所勤務で出向ないところが、優遇であり環境を考慮してるってことだと思います
dialogue.English: I think they believe that working in the office and not having an external assignment *is* the preferential treatment and their way of considering my situation.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。それも納得いかないですよね。今後どんな風になったらいいなと思われますか？
dialogue.English: I understand. That doesn't sit right with you, either. Going forward, how would you like things to be?

dialogue.content: 優しくしてくれる。私の言うことを、そのまま聞いてくれて、そうなるようにしてくれる。
dialogue.English: For them to be kind to me. To listen to what I say, just as I say it, and make it happen.

dialogue.content: ちゃんとしてとか、しっかり聞いてとか言われない
dialogue.English: Not to be told things like 'Do it right' or 'Listen carefully.'

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。そのようになるには、どんな方法が考えらますかね？
dialogue.English: I see. What ways can you think of to make that happen?

dialogue.content: ミスしたら、優しくフォロー、リカバリーしてくれる
dialogue.English: If I make a mistake, for them to gently follow up and help me fix it.

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Mhm.

dialogue.content: そんな方法はないです
dialogue.English: There’s no way to make that happen.

dialogue.content: その方法があれば、相談者様もご納得できますものね。今お辛い現状を誰かに相談できる方は職場にいらっしゃいますか？
dialogue.English: If there were a way, you would feel more settled, wouldn't you? Is there anyone at work you can talk to about this difficult situation?

dialogue.content: バイトに怒られて、我慢して、別部署の人に愚痴言って、慰めてもらうの繰り返し。
dialogue.English: It's a cycle of getting scolded by the part-timers, enduring it, venting to someone in another department, and being comforted.

dialogue.content: 別の部署の方にはお話できるのですね。それだけでも違いますよね。上の方へのお話は難しそうですか？
dialogue.English: So you are able to talk to someone in another department. That in itself must make a difference. Does it seem difficult to talk to your superiors about this?

dialogue.content: 愚痴言ってることが、バレたっぽいけど、バイトの人たちは愚痴言うて息抜きできたらいいやんと言ってた。
dialogue.English: It seems they found out I was venting, but the part-timers said, “It’s fine if venting helps you blow off steam.”

dialogue.content: 上にも愚痴は言ってます。
dialogue.English: I vent to my superiors as well.

dialogue.content: ちゃんとお話しされているのですね。それに対する反応はいかがですか？
dialogue.English: So you are talking to them about it. How do they react?

dialogue.content: ニコニコ笑って聞いてくれてます
dialogue.English: They just listen with a smile on their face.

dialogue.content: 優しいです。
dialogue.English: They're kind.

dialogue.content: 優しい上の方でよかったですね。その反応に、相談者様はどういうお気持ちですか？
dialogue.English: It's good that you have a kind superior. How does their reaction make you feel?

dialogue.content: 優しいですよ
dialogue.English: They are kind.

dialogue.content: その方に、解決の方法を相談するのはどうなのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: What about talking to that person about finding a solution?

dialogue.content: クライアントからクレームなったり、お客様対応が上手くいかなくても、古株のバイトさん達が助けてくれて良かったねって言われます
dialogue.English: When there's a complaint from a client or my customer service doesn't go well, they just say, 'It's a good thing the veteran part-timers were there to help you out.'

dialogue.content: ニコニコ聞いて、そっかぁそうやってフォローしてもらったんやねって言われます
dialogue.English: They listen with a smile and say, 'Oh, I see. So they supported you like that.'

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。そのような状況では、やりきれないですよね。相談者様がどうやったら今よりも不安がなくなるのかについて、もう少し深くかんがえていきたいと思いますので、もしよろしければ、改めてご相談いただけませんか？改めて相談いただいた場合には別の相談員が対応させていただくことになります。その場合でも今日のお話を確認してから相談に乗ることが出来ますので、安心してご利用ください。少しでも相談者様の心が軽くなるお手伝いをさせていただきたいです。
dialogue.English: I see. That must be an unbearable situation. I would like to think more deeply about how we can lessen your anxiety, so if you would be open to it, would you be willing to schedule another consultation? If you do, a different counselor will be assisting you. However, they would review our conversation today before your session, so please rest assured. I would like to help lighten your emotional load, even if just a little.

dialogue.content: はい聞いてくださって有り難うございました
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you for listening to me.

dialogue.content: お話しくださいまして、ありがとうございました。一緒に対応について、また考える機会をいただけますと幸いです。
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing your story with me. I would be grateful for another opportunity to think about solutions together.

dialogue.content: 有り難う
dialogue.English: Thank you

dialogue.content: ございました
dialogue.English: very much.

dialogue.content: （なんかポンコツですみません💦💦評価にてここが良かったや、これだったらもっと良かったなど差し支えなければ具体的に書いていただけると大変助かります！）
dialogue.English: (I’m sorry if I was a bit useless. 💦💦 If it’s not too much trouble, I’d really appreciate it if you could write specific feedback in the evaluation—what was good and what could have been better!)

dialogue.content: (お疲れさまでした。こちらこそ、勉強になりました。有り難うございました。)
dialogue.English: (Thank you for your hard work. This was a learning experience for me as well. Thank you very much.)

dialogue.content: (評価、承知しました。)
dialogue.English: (Understood about the evaluation.)

dialogue.content: （統合が上手くできず。。。打開策が( ;∀;)　もっと勉強しようと思います！ありがとうございました。）
dialogue.English: (I wasn't able to integrate things well... couldn't find a breakthrough ( ;∀;). I'm going to study more! Thank you.)
